definitions.explanation: Engineering work involving the construction of roads, bridges, dams, and other infrastructure. Also refers broadly to construction and earthwork.

examples.japanese: {土木|どぼく}{工事|こうじ}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: The civil engineering work has started.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大学|だいがく}で{土木|どぼく}{工学|こうがく}を{専攻|せんこう}している。
examples.english: He is majoring in civil engineering at university.

examples.japanese: {地震|じしん}の{後|あと}、{道路|どうろ}や{橋|はし}の{復旧|ふっきゅう}のために{大規模|だいきぼ}な{土木|どぼく}{工事|こうじ}が{行|おこな}われた。
examples.english: After the earthquake, large-scale civil engineering work was carried out to restore roads and bridges.

notes:
Composed of {土|ど} (earth, soil) + {木|ぼく} (wood, timber) — the two fundamental materials of traditional construction. In modern usage, it refers specifically to civil engineering as opposed to building construction ({建築|けんちく}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {土木|どぼく}{工事|こうじ} (civil engineering work, construction work)
- {土木|どぼく}{工学|こうがく} (civil engineering as an academic discipline)
- {土木|どぼく}{作業|さぎょう} (construction labor)
- {土木|どぼく}{技術者|ぎじゅつしゃ} (civil engineer)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {建築|けんちく} — architecture, building construction (focuses on buildings)
- {建設|けんせつ} — construction (broader term covering both civil engineering and building)
- インフラ — infrastructure (loanword, refers to the completed systems rather than the engineering work)
